original_question: Let lambda=(lambda_1,...,lambda_n) be eigenvalues with divergent Brjuno-type sum sum_{k>=0} 2^{-k} log(1/Omega_lambda(2^{k+1}))=+infinity, where Omega_lambda(m)=min{|lambda_1^{k_1}...lambda_n^{k_n}-lambda_j|: 2<=k_1+...+k_n<=m, no resonance equality}. Does there exist a germ f in End(C^n,O) with diagonalizable differential having these eigenvalues that is formally linearizable but not holomorphically linearizable?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 1.1, with Proposition 1.2 and Theorem 1.3 giving the paper’s precise proved special case in the setting of only level s resonances.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s central converse-to-Brjuno theme: failure of the relevant Brjuno-type arithmetic condition should force the existence of a germ with the prescribed spectrum that is formally linearizable but not holomorphically linearizable. It also correctly uses the resonant version of the small-divisor function (excluding exact resonances) and asks for a germ whose linear part is diagonalizable with eigenvalues \(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n\).
missing_details: The paper formulates the problem for germs of holomorphic diffeomorphisms/biholomorphisms fixing the origin, not for an arbitrary germ in End(C^n,O). In particular the eigenvalues must lie in (C^*)^n.

The official arithmetic hypothesis is stated as failure of the reduced Brjuno condition, defined using the existence of some strictly increasing sequence \(\{p_\nu\}_{\nu\ge 0}\) with \(p_0=1\), not primarily in the dyadic form appearing in your draft.

Formal linearizability should be spelled out as: there exists a formal change of coordinates tangent to the identity conjugating \(f\) to its linear part \(\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)\).

The paper’s proved result is narrower than your draft: Theorem 1.3 works under an additional resonance restriction ('only level s resonances'), so if you want the paper-faithful proved statement rather than the open conjecture, that restriction must be included.

In the proved special case one must split the spectrum as \(\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_s,\mu_1,\dots,\mu_r)\) with \(1\le s<n\) and \(r=n-s\), and impose the paper’s exact 'only level s resonances' condition.
Proposition 1.2 is part of the nearby context because it reformulates the arithmetic hypothesis in the only-level-s-resonances setting; your draft does not mention that equivalence/reduction.

Theorem 1.3 uses a more specific divergence hypothesis on the first s nonresonant eigenvalues (via the corresponding small-divisor function) than the fully general conjectural failure of the reduced Brjuno condition.

The germ should be stated to fix the origin \(O\), and the differential should be specified as \(df_O=\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)\), not merely 'diagonalizable differential having these eigenvalues'.

The resonance exclusion in the minimum should be described using the paper’s resonance sets \(\operatorname{Res}_j(\lambda)\), i.e. one excludes multi-indices giving a resonance relative to the j-th coordinate.

If the target is the conjecture rather than the theorem, the quantifier is fully general in the spectrum: for every \(\lambda\in (\mathbb C^*)^n\) failing the reduced Brjuno condition, does such a germ exist?
refined_question:
Let \(n\ge 2\) and let \(\lambda=(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)\in(\mathbb C^*)^n\). For \(m\ge 2\), define
\[\widetilde\omega_\lambda(m):=\min_{1\le j\le n}\;\min_{\substack{2\le |Q|\le m\ Q
otin \operatorname{Res}_j(\lambda)}} |\lambda^Q-\lambda_j|,\]
where \(\operatorname{Res}_j(\lambda)=\{Q\in\mathbb N^n:|Q|\ge 2,\ \lambda^Q=\lambda_j\}\). Suppose that \(\lambda\) does not satisfy the reduced Brjuno condition, i.e. there is no strictly increasing sequence \(\{p_
u\}_{
u\ge 0}\) with \(p_0=1\) such that
\[\sum_{
u\ge 0} p_
u^{-1}\log \widetilde\omega_\lambda(p_{
u+1})^{-1}<\infty.\]
Must there exist a germ \(f\in\operatorname{Diff}(\mathbb C^n,0)\) with \(df_0=\operatorname{Diag}(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_n)\) that is formally linearizable (by a formal change of coordinates tangent to the identity) but not holomorphically linearizable?
justification: The draft is aiming at the paper’s main open converse problem: whether failure of the reduced Brjuno condition forces the existence of a formally linearizable but non-holomorphically-linearizable germ with the prescribed diagonalizable linear part. That is the natural content of Conjecture 1.1. The nearby introductory results matter because Proposition 1.2 provides the resonance-adapted reformulation of the arithmetic hypothesis used in the paper’s special setting, and Theorem 1.3 then proves the conjectural phenomenon for spectra having only level s resonances. Your draft is mathematically close, but it omits the paper-critical restrictions distinguishing the open conjecture from the proved special case, and it uses End(C^n,O)/a dyadic sum instead of the paper’s official Diff(C^n,0)/sequence-based reduced Brjuno formulation.
